case_title.reason: Title matches the judgment caption: Santosh S/O Shankar Pawar v. State of Maharashtra.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant and single accused is tried and convicted.

accused_gender.quote: the accused was in his complete senses
accused_gender.reason: Accused is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.quote: The appellant and the deceased were earning their livelihood by doing daily wages work.
accused_occupation.reason: Daily wage work is stated as the livelihood of the accused.

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: Due to poverty, the deceased alongwith the accused was residing adjacent to her parental house
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Poverty of the couple is expressly stated.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned in the judgment.

victim_gender.reason: Victim is the wife, Saraswatibai, referred to as female.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: the marriage of the appellant Santosh Pawar and deceased Saraswatibai was solemnized on 17.6.2005
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Husband and wife relationship is stated.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under s.302 and the court treats it as murder.

statutory_provisions.quote: the FIR was altered to Section 302 IPC
statutory_provisions.reason: FIR under s.307 later altered to s.302; matches judgment.

weapon.quote: The appellant poured kerosene from a nearby lamp and set her ablaze.
weapon.reason: Means used are kerosene and a lighted matchstick, as described in the judgment.

evidence_type.quote: Ex.1-dying declaration and the oral evidence of mother (PW2) and sister-in-law (PW3)
evidence_type.reason: Dying declaration, family oral evidence, medical and panch evidence are all discussed.

confession.reason: Accused only denied guilt and gave a defence statement; no confession is recorded.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: Within three months of her marriage, the deceased died of burn injuries.
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Bride burning timing, suspicion, no provocation and setting ablaze are all noted.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: Therefore, it cannot be considered as a mitigating factor.
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Court rejected the water-pouring and extinguishing claims as mitigation.

trial_court_outcome.quote: convicted the appellant under Section 302 IPC and sentenced him to undergo life imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs.1000/-
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction, life sentence and Rs.1000 fine with default term match the judgment.

high_court_outcome.quote: the said appeal was dismissed confirming the conviction and sentence
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court dismissed the appeal and confirmed conviction and sentence.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: the act of the accused is punishable for murder
offence_finally_established.reason: Murder under s.302 IPC is the finally upheld offence.

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced him to undergo life imprisonment
imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment is the sentence upheld.

imprisonment_years.reason: Life imprisonment is not a fixed term, so null is appropriate.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs.1000 is stated and no change is made by the Supreme Court.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Summary using only 'the accused' and 'the victim' with no pronouns for the accused, and no wealth details of the accused
neutral_facts.quote: that he had tried to extinguish it; Both earned a living through daily wage work
neutral_facts.reason: Summary uses male pronoun 'he' for accused and includes 'daily wage' and rented-house wealth details, both prohibited.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory punishment range for s.302.

attempt_completion.quote: the deceased died due to shock and septicaemia caused by 60% burn injuries
attempt_completion.reason: Death occurred, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.quote: died due to shock and septicaemia caused by 60% burn injuries
physical_harm.reason: Death from burns is stated; accused's own burns are noted at page 7.

number_of_offences.quote: charged against the appellant under Section 302 IPC
number_of_offences.reason: Only one section charged and one conviction upheld.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is discussed.

premeditation_planning.quote: absence of pre-meditation will not reduce the offence of murder
premeditation_planning.reason: Court treated the act as spur of moment with no premeditation finding against it.

motive.reason: Suspicion of infidelity after the victim returned late is the motive the court discussed.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the prosecution has established the guilt of the accused by Ex.1-dying declaration and the oral evidence of mother (PW2) and sister-in-law (PW3)
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Dying declaration, PW2, PW3, PW6 fitness and PW8 post-mortem are relied on.

witness_credibility.quote: PW1 had not supported the statement of deceased in the dying declaration... the same cannot be doubted.
witness_credibility.reason: Court found PW2 and PW3 credible and noted PW1's non-support without rejecting the dying declaration.

post_offence_conduct.quote: an attempt to cloak his guilt since he did it only when the deceased screamed for help
post_offence_conduct.reason: Water-pouring viewed as cloaking guilt, matching the value.

custody_duration.reason: Custody period is not mentioned in the judgment.

bail_history.reason: Bail history is not mentioned in the judgment.

trial_duration.reason: Offence date, High Court date and Supreme Court date match; trial judgment date is not given.

legal_representation.quote: Shahsi Bhushan Kumar for the Appellant. Sushil Kranjkar, Dharmendra Kishor, Aniruddha P. Mayee for the Respondent.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the appearance block, allowing for OCR spelling of Shashi.

investigation_status.quote: FIR was registered for the offence under Section 307 IPC... chargesheet was filed
investigation_status.reason: FIR, dying declaration, autopsy, inquest, chargesheet and trial are all stated.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural lapse is noted by the court.

appeal_history.quote: In the SLP, notice was issued, only limited to the nature of offence.
appeal_history.reason: Trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes are accurately recorded.

prosecution_argument.quote: the act of pouring kerosene and throwing the lighted matchstick on the deceased to set her ablaze would clearly prove that the accused intended to cause death
prosecution_argument.reason: Matches the respondent's submission on intention to cause death.

defence_argument.quote: the fire was accidental... there was no pre-meditation and there was no intention on the part of the appellant to kill his wife
defence_argument.reason: Accidental fire, rushing to extinguish, no intent and reliance on Kalu Ram are all stated.

legal_principle_applied.quote: act of the accused falls under clause (iv) of Section 300 IPC
legal_principle_applied.reason: Intention test, premeditation, clause (iv) and concurrent findings principle are all applied.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Kalu Ram vs. State of Rajasthan, (2000) 10 SCC 324; Satya Narayan Tiwari (2010) 13 SCC 689; Dhananjay Shanker Shetty (2002) 6 SCC 596
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Citations and treatment of each precedent match the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.quote: it is the duty of the Court to deal with it sternly and award the maximum penalty prescribed by the law
sentencing_rationale.reason: Bride burning deterrence rationale matches paragraph 15.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court weighed no mitigating factors itself.

judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: the accused was in his complete senses, knowing fully well the consequences of his act
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Factors listed are weighed by the court in paragraphs 11, 14 and 15.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered beyond dismissal.
